samples.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers base the look on roadside glare, one-handed use and the diary/road-marking idea, and both cover the instructor and learner/parent screens with one shared style. B is more concrete: it gives roles and hex values for status colours, explicit icon guidance, a motion timing, dark mode and a build order. It also invents no prices, while A uses an example price ('Unpaid £45') and a 'block of 10'. A's avoid list pairs a little more clearly with alternatives, and it is tighter. Neither answer gives proper system font fallbacks, and A actually tells the tool not to use system defaults. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers draw their direction from the roadside, glare and one-handed use, and keep the driving motifs restrained. A is more complete to paste: it gives status colours with roles, a dark mode, explicit icon guidance and a clearer contrast target. B adds useful touches like offline status and the rival-name check, but it brings in invented specifics such as 'Unpaid £45' and 'block of 10'. Neither gives proper system font fallbacks.

pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A ties more of its choices to how Clutchpoint is used: glare at the roadside, one thumb, weak signal, and a diary or logbook for reference. It keeps the driving motif to a single 'bite point' notch and points out its own assumptions about payment and offline saving. Answer B gives slightly more exact values, such as border widths, spacing and motion timing, and adds useful process steps. However, it leans harder on the road-sign look with uppercase labels and a hard offset shadow, and it assumes lesson length and price appear in booking slots. Neither answer gives a system font fallback. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both briefs share a strong core: a warm paper background, near-black ink and one amber or yellow accent, ruled rows instead of cards, a bottom action bar within thumb reach, one-tap Mark done with Undo, and offline saving. B ties its choices more closely to how instructors actually work, for example showing last lesson's notes and changing the main action from Start to Mark done to Take payment. It keeps the driving motif light by using the bite-point notch in one place only, bans invented stats and sample data, and tells the user which assumptions to check. A is tighter and very pasteable, but it uses all-caps labels and a hard offset shadow, and its ban list pairs fewer items with alternatives. Neither brief gives system font fallbacks, and B mislabels the 7:1 contrast ratio as WCAG AA when it is the AAA level.

pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers ground the look in roadside phone use and give concrete colours, type, shape and layout rules, and both cover the instructor and learner/parent sides with one shared look. B goes further on things instructors actually hit: poor signal, failed payments, no-shows and an edit-ready skill vocabulary. It also flags its currency and terms as guesses to swap out. A states invented facts as given (a £40 lesson price and a 90-second window between lessons) and leans a little harder on car costume (number plates). Neither answer gives system font fallbacks. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both briefs are concrete and grounded in the roadside phone use, with ledger-style rows instead of cards, a light theme for glare and one yellow accent. B gives more detail in places, including a secondary grey, an elevation rule, a voice section and a navigation limit, but it invents facts: an '~90 seconds' gap between lessons, '£40' and the learner name 'Sam'. A avoids invented facts, uses '£__' and says which choices are guesses, and covers more of the learner/parent flow and the edge cases (offline sync, failed payment, no-show).
